notes: The copula was given to the fronted prepositional predicate under rule 49; giving it to the nominal 'an army' was the competing reading, rejected because the Hebrew clause predicates the prepositional phrase of the army.
'chel tsava' is rendered by the single word 'army', so the two nouns share one unit headed on tsava, which carries the lexeme (rule 30); the Hebrew gloss note corroborates and decides nothing.
The second lamed before 'the king' is unrepresented, its object being rendered as the bare object of 'help' (rule 40).
